short: A highly successful Shokaku-class carrier, Zuikaku participated in nearly every major Pacific fleet action before her destruction.
full:
Commissioned in late 1941, Zuikaku was one of the most advanced and capable aircraft carriers of the Imperial Japanese Navy. Alongside her sister ship Shokaku, she formed the Fifth Carrier Division and took part in the attack on Pearl Harbor. Known for her remarkable luck in escaping early battles undamaged, Zuikaku fought at the Coral Sea, the Eastern Solomons, and the Santa Cruz Islands.

As the war turned against Japan and her elite aviators were lost, Zuikaku's effectiveness waned. During the Battle of Leyte Gulf in October 1944, she served as a sacrificial decoy to draw the American fast carrier task force away from the main Japanese surface fleet. She was overwhelmed by American aircraft at the Battle off Cape Engaño and sank, taking the last vestige of the Pearl Harbor strike force with her.
